section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The 2D Area Intuition
section_1.content: Briefly define the 2D determinant as the signed area of a parallelogram spanned by two vectors. Establish that scaling vectors changes the area proportionally.
section_1.example: Imagine two 'vector sticks' on a table forming a shadow. If you stretch one stick, the shadow area grows linearly.

section_2.title: Defining the Cross Product via the Parallelogram
section_2.content: Transition to 3D space. Define the cross product as a vector whose magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram formed by two vectors, and whose direction is perpendicular (Right-Hand Rule).
section_2.example: Visualize a robotic arm's two joints; the cross product magnitude represents the 'swept area' the arm covers during a swing.

section_3.title: The Linear Transformation Link: Determinants in 3D
section_3.content: Explain that the cross product is inherently linked to the 3D determinant (the scalar triple product). It measures how a linear transformation changes the volume of a unit cube.
section_3.example: An animation showing a 'cube of jelly' being squashed or stretched by a matrix; the cross product helps calculate the surface normal of the cube's faces.

section_4.title: Geometric Application: The Normal Vector
section_4.content: Demonstrate why the cross product is the tool of choice for finding surface normals—critical for lighting in computer graphics and physics simulations.
section_4.example: A 3D character (e.g., a cyber-fox) standing in a game engine; the cross product calculates the surface normal of its fur triangles to determine how light reflects off them.

section_5.title: Summary: The 'Flow' of Cross Products
section_5.content: Recap: Cross product = Magnitude (Area) + Direction (Normal). It is the bridge between vector geometry and the volumetric perspective of linear algebra.
section_5.example: A quick visual montage: From two lines forming a plane, to the orthogonal vector shooting out, to the lighting engine calculating the final pixel color.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The 2D Area Intuition",

        label_h = MathTex("h", color="#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, "C3")
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(area_fill, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(area_fill))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(area_fill))
        self.wait(1)
